blockMcqs.question: What is the primary guarantee of a transaction?
options: All operations succeed or none take effect
blockMcqs.explanation: A transaction is all-or-nothing — partial success is never visible to the outside world.

blockMcqs.question: In a money transfer, why must debit and credit be one transaction?
options: To let other users see the balance sooner
So a crash cannot leave one side applied without the other
Transactions are required by SQL syntax
blockMcqs.explanation: Without a single transaction, a crash between the two writes leaves the account debited but never credited.

blockMcqs.question: Which mechanism lets a database undo a half-finished transaction?
blockMcqs.explanation: An undo log records the before-images of modified rows so the DB can reverse them if the transaction fails.

blockMcqs.question: What anomaly does Isolation prevent when two transactions withdraw simultaneously?
options: Both reading a stale balance and both succeeding
blockMcqs.explanation: Without isolation, two concurrent withdrawals read the same balance and both pass, overdrawing the account.

blockMcqs.question: How does a database guarantee Durability after COMMIT?
options: Keeping data only in RAM until shutdown
Flushing changes to a write-ahead log before acknowledging
Replicating to all read replicas before responding
Running a VACUUM after each transaction
blockMcqs.explanation: WAL ensures changes land on disk before the DB confirms the commit, so a crash cannot lose them.

blockMcqs.question: Last SQL done, not yet flushed to disk — which transaction state?
blockMcqs.explanation: Partially committed means all operations are done but the flush to durable storage has not yet completed.

blockMcqs.question: Can a committed transaction be undone with ROLLBACK?
options: Only if no other transaction read it
blockMcqs.explanation: COMMIT makes changes permanent and visible; there is no undo. A new compensating transaction is the only recourse.

blockMcqs.question: Who issues ROLLBACK if the application crashes mid-transaction?
blockMcqs.explanation: On restart, the DB replays its log and rolls back any transaction that had not committed before the crash.
